title: Four Triangle Restaurants Make Yelp's First Top 100 Indian List in the US
excerpt: Lime & Lemon in Chapel Hill ranks No. 18 nationally, joined by Raleigh's Bombay Curry, Masala House and Mustang House on the review-driven list Yelp describes as its first.
body:
• Four Triangle restaurants appear on the Top 100 Indian Restaurants list for the United States that Yelp describes as its first-ever such ranking: Lime & Lemon in Chapel Hill (No. 18), Bombay Curry in Raleigh (No. 41), Masala House in Raleigh (No. 65) and Mustang House in Raleigh (No. 72).
  • North Carolina placed eight restaurants on the national list in total — the others are in Charlotte, Burlington, Asheville and Winston-Salem.
  • Yelp ranked businesses in its Indian category on review ratings and volume, capping the list at 10 restaurants per state; all listed restaurants had a passing health score.
  • Planning a visit: Bombay Curry is at 13220 Strickland Rd, Suite 167, Raleigh, and Mustang House at 411 Fayetteville St, Suite 109, Raleigh — check the list before you go, because national-list weekends get busy.

Four Indian restaurants in North Carolina's Triangle have made Yelp's Top 100 Indian Restaurants list for the United States — a national ranking built from diner reviews that puts a Chapel Hill grill at No. 18 and three Raleigh restaurants inside the top 75.

The Triangle's four

The highest-ranked Triangle entry is Lime & Lemon – Chapel Hill at No. 18 nationally. The restaurant, in Chapel Hill's Meadowmont Village, is the Chapel Hill outpost of a small group that also serves Raleigh and Durham, and its menu runs from mango lime chicken to the standard North Indian canon.

Raleigh contributes the other three. Bombay Curry (No. 41), at 13220 Strickland Rd, Suite 167 in North Raleigh, is a long-running neighbourhood spot whose tandoor dishes anchor its reviews. Masala House comes in at No. 65, and Mustang House (No. 72), at 411 Fayetteville St, Suite 109 in downtown Raleigh, stands out on the list for its momos — the Nepali dumplings get their own section of its menu.

How the list was built

Yelp said it identified businesses in its Indian restaurant category and ranked them on factors including the total volume of reviews and their ratings, according to USA Today's publication of the full list. To widen the map, Yelp capped entries at 10 per state, and listed restaurants held a passing health score as of August 11, 2026. California took the maximum 10 places, including No. 1, LA Indian Cuisine in Castaic. North Carolina's eight entries also include Curry Gate 2 in Charlotte (No. 32), Curry Palace in Burlington (No. 67), Mehfil in Asheville (No. 76) and Curry and Noodle in Winston-Salem (No. 100).

"Our first-ever Top 100 Indian Restaurants list is all about hospitality, comfort, and creativity. Yelpers say they feel like guests in someone's home at many of these restaurants."

— Tara Lewis, Yelp trend expert, via USA Today

Why it matters here

The Triangle's Indian dining scene has grown with the region's Indian population, and a review-driven national list is a different kind of recognition from a critic's award: it measures how often ordinary diners come back and what they say afterwards. Yelp's accompanying trend data points the same way — the platform reported searches for Indian food buffets up 437% and for Indian tiffin services up 76% in its 2026 food trend report. For readers in the Raleigh-Durham area, the actionable version of this story is short: four of the country's most-reviewed Indian restaurants are within a local drive, and two of them are on Strickland Road and Fayetteville Street in Raleigh.
nri_angle: For the Triangle's large Indian community, the list is both recognition and a practical shortlist — four nationally ranked Indian restaurants within a local drive of Morrisville and Cary.
